verdict.headline: Alphabet heads for its worst post-earnings drop and pulls tech futures lower before inflation data
verdict.label: Pre-market: Nasdaq-100 futures -1.0% to -1.3%, S&P 500 futures about -0.5%, Dow futures about +0.3%; Alphabet about -10%, Microsoft about +3.5%; 10Y ~5.00%–5.04%; Brent $114.30; DXY ~102.2; BTC $80,072.
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: Alphabet is down about 10% before the open, on course for its worst post-earnings reaction if it closes more than 9.77% lower. Free cash flow of negative $9.07 billion was more than three times the negative $2.70 billion expected, and search advertising missed. Nasdaq-100 futures are down 1.0%–1.3% and chip makers are lower, while Microsoft is up about 3.5% and Dow futures are higher.

What it means: the market is selling the company carrying the cost of AI building, not AI demand: Google Cloud grew 103% and Alphabet kept its $195–$205 billion capex plan. Chip makers are falling with Alphabet's shares even though that plan is their revenue, so the evidence for suppliers cuts both ways.

What would change the picture: a Nasdaq close back above 26,424.82, or Amazon's results tonight being rewarded for higher spending, would undo the read. September PCE at 8:30am, expected at 3.6% headline and 3.1% core, decides whether the 10-year tests 5.11% on top of the earnings selling.
verdict.lede_short: Alphabet is down about 10% before the open, on course for its worst post-earnings drop, after free cash flow came in at negative $9.07 billion and search ads missed, and Nasdaq futures are down about 1% while Microsoft rises. The market is selling the cost of AI building, not the demand: cloud grew 103%. PCE at 8:30am and Amazon tonight decide whether the Nasdaq gets back above 26,424.82 or the 10-year tests 5.11%.

supporting_data.label: Alphabet fell about 10% premarket and would post its worst post-earnings reaction on record with a close more than 9.77% lower — a move of that size erases roughly $400 billion of market value.

Alphabet's free cash flow of negative $9.07 billion was more than three times the negative $2.70 billion expected, and search advertising grew 12% to $63.35 billion, short of forecasts — the business that funds the spending missed in the quarter the spending deepened the cash burn.

Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 1.3% and S&P 500 futures 0.5% while Dow futures rose 0.3%, with Microsoft up 3.5% on 48% Azure growth — the selling is concentrated in AI spenders and suppliers, not spread across the market.
AMD fell 3.3%, Intel 3.6% and Nvidia about 1% in early premarket trading — chip makers are trading with Alphabet's share price rather than with the capex plan that pays them.

September PCE is expected at 3.6% headline and 3.1% core, with third-quarter GDP near 3.2%, both at 8:30am — with the 10-year near 5% and December hike odds at 85.7%, a hot print would add rate pressure to tech selling.
Brent fell 0.86% to $114.30 after reports that Vice President Vance contacted Iranian officials — oil gave back part of Wednesday's gain, taking some pressure off long yields before PCE.

watchlist_mentions.note: Down about 10% premarket; a close more than 9.77% lower would be its worst post-earnings reaction on record.
Up about 3.5% premarket on 48% Azure growth and capex below forecasts.
Down about 3.3% in early premarket trading with chip makers after Alphabet's results.
Down about 1% in early premarket trading, less than other chip makers.
Reports after the close with about $202.2 billion of revenue and $1.96 of EPS expected; capex guidance stands at $220 billion.
At $80,072, under the $80,320 October 8 low after an overnight low of $79,623.

trade_setups.thesis: Nasdaq-100 futures are down 1.0%–1.3% on Alphabet's cash burn; a 1% decline at the open would put the Composite near 26,285, under this week's breakout level, before Amazon reports tonight.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back above 26,424.82, or Amazon's results being rewarded for higher spending, would undo the read; a close under 26,169.38 would erase this week's gain.

trade_setups.thesis: The 10-year is near 5% ahead of September PCE, expected at 3.6% headline and 3.1% core, with December hike odds at 85.7%.
trade_setups.invalidation: A print above expectations would test 5.11%; a softer print would likely take the 10-year back under 5%.
trade_setups.horizon: Through the 8:30am PCE and GDP release

trade_setups.thesis: Bitcoin is at $80,072, under its $80,320 October 8 low, falling 1.3% in step with Nasdaq futures.
trade_setups.invalidation: A recovery above $80,320 by Friday's monthly options expiry would make this a test that held; a daily close under $79,623 would put the low in question.
